newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian gilts slump, market awaits stock auction.
newsitem.headline: Indian gilts slump, market awaits stock auction.

text.p: Indian call rates ended Tuesday at 0.50-0.75 percent, barely changed from the day's opening quotes on good liquidity and poor demand, dealers said.
They said rates were largely stuck in a 0.50-0.75 percent band through most of the day with a few stray deals struck at 1.0 percent in late afternoon.
Market attention was focussed on a security auction slated for April 30, dealers said.
State government bonds worth 25 billion rupees, with a 10-year maturity, are auctioned by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) on Wednesday.
Dealers said they expected the auction to attract bids in excess of the target amount and the RBI to retain part or all of the excess.
"We are waiting to see the response to the auction," said a dealer at a state-run bank. "We expect outflows towards the loan to be around 40 billion rupees.
"This could push call money rates up to 2.0 percent," he said. "But it depends how much of the excess bids the RBI chooses to retain."
Security prices fell on selling pressure as buyers stayed away ahead of the auction, dealers said.
"Fresh positions will be taken after Wednesday," said a dealer.
Dealers said a leading insurance company sold short-term securities worth 1.70 billion rupees.
This contributed substantially to trades rising to 3.80 billion rupees against Monday's 2.49 billion, dealers said.
Dealers said primary dealers sold a newly-auctioned 10-year government of India stock.

"It appears that they are looking to switch to the state loan stock tomorrow," said a dealer. "At the moment they can sell the 10-year 13.05 percent stock around 101.20 rupees while tomorrow's issue at the same coupon is at par."
"This seems to have led to quite a bit of selling in the 13.05 percent 2007 today," he said.
The 13.05 percent 2007 stock fell to 101.20 rupees, compared to 101.45 rupees, dealers said. "It was traded at 101.40 rupees and 101.32 rupees, before trading at 101.20 rupees," they said.

The 13.50 percent 1997 stock fell to 101.95 rupees from its previous close of 102.15 rupees, the 13.50 percent 1998 stock to 103.20 rupees from 103.50 rupees and the 13.40 percent 1999 to 105.80 rupees from 106.30, dealers said.
Dealers said three-month commercial paper was quoted in a 9.5-10.5 percent range in the primary market.
